features.name: share_comments_with_epistemic_hedge
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments contain an epistemic hedge phrase such as "I think", "I believe" or "in my view"?
features.spec: Parse df['OC_comments'] as a JSON list of strings; malformed/missing -> null; empty list -> null. For each comment, case-insensitive regex match with word boundaries for the literal hedge phrases: "i think", "i believe", "in my view" (also allow curly apostrophes not needed). Output = (number of comments matching at least one phrase) / (total number of comments). Raw text matching: matches inside quotations of others or in comments containing outcome announcements are still counted; no semantic filtering.

h0: share_comments_with_epistemic_hedge has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: A higher share_comments_with_epistemic_hedge is associated with a lower probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Hedge phrase list is limited to the three examples given; other hedges (e.g. "maybe", "I feel") are not counted. Row-level share of comments is used, so comment-level persuasiveness is not measured (no per-comment outcomes). Matches may occur in quoted text or in comments mentioning the outcome (contamination risk); raw text is not outcome-free. Comment order/timing unknown. Rows with empty comment lists yield null.
